reason: The first reading of the abraded strips was revised against Graesse's text to fix expansions and line-joins in the Simon notice and the magi dispute, and to read the All Saints rubric and opening.
sources: Th. Graesse, Jacobi a Voragine Legenda aurea, 2nd ed. 1850, cap. 159 pp. 709-711 (page images of pp. 709 and 711; OCR of p. 710) and cap. 162 p. 718 (OCR), archive.org legendaaureavulg00jacouoft and bub_gb_h2rkGCFC1G0C
Iacobus de Voragine, Legenda aurea, ed. G. P. Maggioni, Simon and Jude and All Saints chapters, Corpus Corporum (search snippets)
Iohannes Aegidii Zamorensis, Legende sanctorum, Simon notice, Corpus Corporum (search snippets; tested as an alternative)
text:
Source-assisted reading of F-nbxz (Stams, Stiftsarchiv, Frg. 64), made with Graesse's Legenda aurea (1850) at hand. Reread on native images by a research reader: canvas 0 second column, lines 1-14; canvas 1 first column, lines 1-14 (middles of lines). Canvas 1 second-column line-beginnings and canvas 0 first-column line-ends are the image-only first reading, checked against the crops. Regions are x,y,width,height in native pixels. Expansions are in ( ), [..] marks lost letters, ? marks an uncertain reading, | marks a cut between strips.
